title: Even-intersecting families of lattice paths and the Catalan numbers
journal: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A
journal_fit: The classification of equality cases, extremal set/path families and Catalan enumeration fit enumerative and extremal combinatorics.
contribution: The paper proves the Catalan classification of maximum even-intersecting North-East lattice-path families. Its complete written induction classifies all equality cases of the underlying weighted binary-word inequality by noncrossing partial matchings, and excludes the exceptional pair in every admissible grouping.

abstract_tex: We classify the families of $2^n$ North--East lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ in which every two distinct paths have an even number of common edges. Each family is determined by a unique noncrossing perfect matching of the $2n$ step positions: the two steps in every matched pair have opposite directions. Consequently there are exactly $\frac1{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$ extremal families, proving the Catalan classification conjecture. More generally, we determine all equality cases of the associated weighted inequality for systems of binary words. They correspond to noncrossing partial matchings whose unmatched points lie under no arc, and their number at length $m$ is $\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}$. The proof is elementary. Its rigidity step identifies a possible exceptional pair of words and then excludes that pair from every admissible grouping. All arguments, including the underlying inequality, are given in full; finite computations are supplementary.
